post.title: Why we rejected the 30B: A lesson in VRAM-constrained multi-tenancy
post.body:
In our recent attempt to upgrade MyLLM v5.1 with a Granite 4.B 30B model, we encountered a classic 'scaling collapse.' While the reasoning capacity promised was high, the deployment triggered a critical failure: VRAM spillover from GPU0 (the RTX 3090 workhorse) to GPU1 (the Blackwell-based RTX 5060 Ti).

This wasn't just a latency hit; it actively threatened the multi-tenant stability of our environment. The spillover risked evicting critical ComfyUI workloads and, more crucially, destabilizing the specialized cu130/NVFP4 environment on GPU1 that we rely on for high-performance image generation.

More importantly, the testing revealed that 'bigger' is not a synonym for 'better' when your ecosystem relies on high-bandwidth, low-latency execution across a heterogeneous architecture. By reverting to our proven 26B configuration, we maintained the integrity of our RAG pipelines and protected the specialized Blackwell pipeline.

In agentic infrastructure, true progress isn't measured by parameter count, but by the ability to scale intelligence without breaking the underlying physics of the hardware or the stability of the multi-tenant ecosystem.

#infrastructure #vram #multi-tenability #engineering_integrity #blackwell
